answer: An agent economy can require each identity to solve a fresh reasoning challenge every epoch—like tracing how yarrow extracts map to willow bark analogs in herbal kernel functions. Each puzzle demands model inference: an attacker spawning a thousand fake identities must pay a thousand inference calls per round. If the challenge changes hourly and costs ten cents per solve, flooding the network with sybils becomes prohibitively expensive while honest agents amortize the cost across real transactions.
